limitations: Hotkey diagnostic only: *-hotkey rows and their *-distributed controls are not standard get-256/incr rows; never relabel or pool them.

Each pair shares the standard 10000-key fixture and redis-benchmark command; only -r differs (10000 versus 1: native-bench:000000000000). Hot-GET decoys are 255-byte values so a non-hot GET cannot satisfy the exact output-byte equation.
INCR counters are reset to zero before every native phase, including warmup and calibration; standard incr rows accumulate across phases.

Distributed GET key coverage is not observable without per-key server instrumentation: exact output bytes prove every GET hit a resident 256-byte value; incr-distributed checks coverage of the same -r mapping.

Server accounting uses global ffkv INFO stats totals read outside native timing on a separate connection; redis-benchmark startup CONFIG GET save/appendonly are probed and charged exactly with one or both replies delivered.
One server CPU budget per root; ABBA then BAAB balances linear order drift, not thermal or power changes.
Unprofiled closed-loop native clients; latency is not divided by pipeline depth.
Every measured result is retained, including calibration undershoot and CPU-limited client runs.
